--- title: "Spatial Analysis and Stage-to-Stage Change" subtitle: "Hotspot structure of fishing activity across three phases of offshore wind development" --- ## Question Does the spatial structure of fishing activity change across the three development stages, and does it change differently for mobile and fixed gear? The analysis runs entirely on open-source tools — `geopandas`, `libpysal`, `esda` — replacing an ArcGIS chain that could not be reproduced without a Pro licence. Every spatial input is committed to the repository; the Global Fishing Watch extracts are gitignored and regenerated by the R pull. ::: {#setup .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import warnings, logging warnings.filterwarnings("ignore") logging.basicConfig(level=logging.ERROR) import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import numpy as np import pandas as pd from gfw_fishing_osw_ais import ( aggregate, config as cfg, io, spatial_stats as ss, transitions as tr, viz, weights as wts ) grid = io.load_grid() owf = io.load_owf() aoi = io.load_aoi() pd.set_option("display.width", 200) ``` ::: ## Methods ### Spatial support The analysis grid is 3,375 cells at 0.01°, projected to UTM 19N (EPSG:32619), covering the Ørsted AOI. Records are joined to cells with `geopandas.sjoin` and rolled up per cell per stage: $$\text{MonthMean}_i = \frac{\sum_j h_{ij}}{M_s}$$ where $h_{ij}$ are hours in cell $i$ and $M_s$ is the number of months in stage $s$ (44 / 43 / 40). The denominator is the *stage* length, not the number of months that cell was active, so zero-inflation is structural. Statistics run on $\sqrt{\text{MonthMean}}$, chosen on the evidence in `01-data-exploration.qmd`. ### Spatial weights ::: {.callout-warning} ## Geometric contiguity is unusable on this grid The grid was built by drawing an independent 0.01° square around each GFW point and reprojecting with `PRESERVE_SHAPE`, so adjacent cells do not share exact vertices. `Queen.from_dataframe` returns **1.96 mean neighbours across 74 disconnected components**, which would render every local statistic meaningless. ::: Contiguity is instead derived analytically from the lattice indices the shapefile already carries. Two cells are Queen neighbours iff their integer indices differ by at most one on each axis — no geometry predicate, no tolerance. ::: {#tbl-weights .cell tbl-cap='Neighbour-count distribution of the lattice-derived Queen weights' execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} w = wts.lattice_queen(grid) w_star = wts.gi_star_weights(grid) wts.validate_weights(w) wts.neighbor_summary(w) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
n_neighbors n_cells pct_cells
0 4 43 1.3
1 5 128 3.8
2 6 35 1.0
3 7 62 1.8
4 8 3107 92.1
``` ::: ::: ::: {#weights-summary .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} print(f"n = {w.n}, mean neighbours = {w.mean_neighbors:.2f}, " f"components = {w.n_components}, islands = {len(w.islands)}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` n = 3375, mean neighbours = 7.80, components = 1, islands = 0 ``` ::: ::: Validated three ways: `validate_weights` rejects the geometric construction it guards against; all 26,312 neighbour pairs lie within one cell diagonal (max 1,395 m against a legal 1,424 m), so no false links are created; and the relation is perfectly symmetric. ### Statistics | Purpose | Method | Inference | |---|---|---| | Global clustering | `esda.Moran` | analytic | | Global high/low | `esda.G` | analytic | | Local hotspots (Gi\*) | `esda.G_Local`, **binary weights** | analytic, BH-FDR | | Local clusters/outliers | `esda.Moran_Local`, 999 permutations, seeded | conditional randomisation, BH-FDR | Two points of care, both documented in `00b-plan-revisions.qmd`: **Gi\* requires binary weights.** Its variance depends on the weight sum $W_i$; row standardisation forces $W_i = 1$ and compresses every z-score. On these data that is the difference between max |z| of 10.78 and 3.96 — between 832 significant cells and none. `esda.G_Local` defaults to `transform="R"` and re-standardises in place, so the call site passes `transform="B"`. **Permutations are seeded** (`cfg.RANDOM_SEED = 42`). The archived workflow set no seed and its Local Moran's results were therefore not reproducible. ::: {#run-analysis .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} cells_afe, glob_afe = ss.run_all("afe") cells_vp, glob_vp = ss.run_all("vp") trans_afe = tr.run_transitions("afe", cells_afe, grid) trans_vp = tr.run_transitions("vp", cells_vp, grid) ``` ::: ## Global spatial autocorrelation ::: {#tbl-global .cell tbl-cap='Global Moran\'s I on the sqrt surfaces, all gear' execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = pd.concat([glob_vp, glob_afe]).query("gear_class == 'ALL'") g[["dataset", "stage", "n_active", "morans_i", "morans_z", "morans_p", "general_g_z", "n_hot", "n_cold"]] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Vessel presence is strongly clustered and near-constant across stages. **Apparent fishing effort clusters progressively more strongly** — 0\.347 → 0\.416 → 0\.495 — meaning fishing effort concentrates spatially as development proceeds, even as total mobile-gear effort returns to baseline. ::: {#cell-fig-moran .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4)) for ds, glob, color in (("vp", glob_vp, "#2166ac"), ("afe", glob_afe, "#b2182b")): sub = glob.query("gear_class == 'ALL'").sort_values("stage") ax.plot([cfg.STAGES[s].label for s in sub.stage], sub.morans_i, "o-", color=color, linewidth=2, markersize=8, label=cfg.DATASETS[ds].label) ax.set_ylabel("Global Moran's I") ax.set_ylim(0, 0.8) ax.legend(frameon=False) ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False) plt.tight_layout() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Global Moran's I by stage. Fishing effort concentrates; vessel presence does not.](02-spatial-analysis_files/figure-html/fig-moran-output-1.png){#fig-moran width=1101 height=624} ::: ::: ## Hotspot structure by stage ::: {#cell-fig-gi-afe .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig = viz.reference_strip("afe", cells_afe, grid, owf, aoi) plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Getis-Ord Gi* hotspots, apparent fishing effort, by development stage. Ørsted lease areas outlined.](02-spatial-analysis_files/figure-html/fig-gi-afe-output-1.png){#fig-gi-afe width=1773 height=736} ::: ::: ## Stage-to-stage change Three maps read side by side ask a viewer to hold one in working memory while scanning the next. The change maps do that differencing explicitly. ::: {#cell-fig-hero-afe .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig = viz.hero_figure("afe", trans_afe, grid, owf, aoi) plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Change in apparent-fishing-effort hotspot structure across both stage transitions.](02-spatial-analysis_files/figure-html/fig-hero-afe-output-1.png){#fig-hero-afe width=1906 height=1170} ::: ::: ::: {#tbl-change-afe .cell tbl-cap='Stage 2 to Stage 3 change in hotspot classification, all gear' execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} trans_afe[(2, 3, None)]["summary"] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=10} ```{=html}

There is **no statistical test of the difference between two Gi\* surfaces**. Read them as description, not as a significance test of change. ::: ## The gear comparison ::: {#cell-fig-gear-afe .cell execution_count=12} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig = viz.gear_small_multiples("afe", trans_afe, grid, owf, aoi) plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Stage 2 to Stage 3 change by gear class. Mobile contracts slightly; fixed expands substantially.](02-spatial-analysis_files/figure-html/fig-gear-afe-output-1.png){#fig-gear-afe width=1801 height=782} ::: ::: ::: {#tbl-gear-change .cell tbl-cap='Net hotspot area change, Stage 2 to Stage 3, by gear class' execution_count=13} ``` {.python .cell-code} rows = [] for gc in (None,) + cfg.ANALYSIS_GEAR_CLASSES: key = (2, 3, gc) if key not in trans_afe: continue s = trans_afe[key]["summary"].set_index("change") rows.append({ "gear_class": gc or "ALL", "gained hot km2": s.loc["gained hot", "area_km2"], "lost hot km2": s.loc["lost hot", "area_km2"], "net km2": round(s.loc["gained hot", "area_km2"] - s.loc["lost hot", "area_km2"], 1), }) pd.DataFrame(rows) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=13} ```{=html}

Spatially, mobile-gear hotspots sit on the western margin of the AOI, largely outside the lease areas. Fixed-gear hotspots expand around and into the lease perimeter. ## Activity inside the lease areas The hotspot maps show where activity concentrates. This asks the blunter question of whether it happens inside the lease footprints at all. ::: {#tbl-lease-afe .cell tbl-cap='Apparent fishing effort inside the lease polygons versus elsewhere in the AOI' execution_count=15} ``` {.python .cell-code} lease_afe = tr.lease_share("afe") lease_afe.query("gear_class in ['ALL', 'MOBILE', 'FIXED']") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=15} ```{=html}

Effort inside is flat; growth happens entirely outside.](02-spatial-analysis_files/figure-html/fig-lease-output-1.png){#fig-lease width=1184 height=624} ::: ::: ## Synthesis {#sec-synthesis} ### The aggregate increase is mostly not real Apparent fishing effort rises 147\.5 → 186\.2 → 230\.4 hours per month across stages. But the tracked fleet grows 152 → 178 → 216 vessels, and **effort per vessel-month is essentially flat at 0\.97 → 1\.05 → 1\.07**. Nearly all of the headline increase is AIS coverage expanding, not fishing intensifying. Vessel presence behaves the same way (0\.82 → 0\.88 → 0\.94). This is the most important framing constraint in the analysis. Any statement of the form "fishing effort increased during construction" is, on these data, largely a statement about AIS adoption. ### The real signal is gear divergence, and it replicates | hours per vessel-month | Stage 1 | Stage 2 | Stage 3 | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Mobile — effort | 1\.28 | 1\.56 | **1\.20** | | Fixed — effort | 1\.03 | 0\.87 | **1\.78** | | Mobile — presence | 1\.05 | 1\.12 | **1\.02** | | Fixed — presence | 0\.92 | 1\.19 | **2\.18** | Fixed gear intensifies per vessel in **both independent measures** while mobile returns to baseline in both. Fixed-gear effort grows 4\.3× in absolute terms on a fleet that only grew from 10 to 25 vessels. Coverage growth would lift both gear types equally, so this is a behavioural difference rather than a sampling artifact. ### The fishery grew around the leases, not inside them Effort inside the lease footprints is **flat in absolute terms** — 39\.5 → 35\.7 → 33\.6 hours per month — while effort elsewhere in the AOI nearly doubles, 108\.0 → 150\.6 → 196\.8. The in-lease share therefore falls from 26\.8% to 14\.6%. That distinction matters: this is relative displacement, not absolute abandonment. Mobile gear shows the clearest withdrawal, its in-lease share falling 28\.7% → 18\.9% → 16\.5%. Vessel presence does the opposite. Presence inside the leases *rises* (96.5 → 102.9 → 128.0 hours per month) on a roughly constant share. **Vessels increasingly move through the lease areas without fishing in them.** Structurally, Global Moran's I for effort climbs 0\.347 → 0\.416 → 0\.495 — activity concentrates into a consolidated band along the western AOI margin. Net hotspot area change from Stage 2 to Stage 3 is −9\.2 km² for mobile against \+140\.5 km² for fixed. ## Caveats on the interpretation **This is not a causal design.** There is no control area and no before-after-control-impact structure. Displacement, shifting stock distribution, regulatory change and fuel prices are not separable here. The analysis describes what changed in this AOI over this period; it does not attribute that change to wind development. **Apparent fishing effort is a model output**, not observed fishing. GFW infers it from vessel behaviour, and the inference itself may perform differently around construction activity. **The unresolved class expands most of all** (\+190\.9 km² net, 258\.0 gained against 67\.1 lost) and is not interpretable as a gear signal — it reflects GFW registry coverage. Some genuine mobile and fixed activity sits in that panel. It is shown rather than hidden for exactly that reason. **Eleven offshore-wind charter and research vessels were removed** beyond the 35 on Ørsted's own list, after they were found driving an apparent fishing-effort increase inside the Revolution Wind lease. Eight were identified by a behavioural screen rather than confirmed by registry evidence. Before that correction the analysis showed mobile effort flat and a 448 km² cold-spot region that does not exist. The screen also cannot detect an established fishing vessel that takes a charter — the *Virginia Wave* escaped the first pass for exactly that reason. Full detail in `00b-plan-revisions.qmd`. **AIS coverage grows across the study period**, so absolute hours are not comparable between stages without the per-vessel normalisation reported above. **The transition tables describe, they do not test.** Each surface is FDR-corrected within its own stage; there is no significance test of the difference between two surfaces. **Local Moran's `LL` counts are unreliable for sparse gear classes**, where they are dominated by the structural zero field rather than by meaningful low-activity clusters. Gi\* is the more trustworthy statistic on those surfaces — it reports no cold spots there, correctly, since a cell cannot sit significantly below a floor of zero. ## Why this matters **Fisheries displacement is the central socioeconomic question in US offshore wind permitting, and it is chronically evidence-poor.** Federal decisions and the compensation frameworks in Rhode Island and Massachusetts rest largely on stated-preference surveys and self-reported vessel trip reports. This provides an independent, spatially explicit, reproducible measure built from a public data source. **The gear-specific result has direct management implications.** Mobile and fixed gear are not interchangeable in mitigation design — turbine spacing, cable burial and transit corridors affect a trawler and a pot boat differently. Evidence that fixed-gear activity intensified while mobile withdrew argues against uniform mitigation, and speaks to which fleet segments bear the cost. **The charter-vessel finding generalises well beyond this project.** Offshore wind developers charter commercial fishing hulls as scout and safety vessels. Those vessels retain their fishing registry classification, so GFW records their project work as apparent fishing effort — concentrated inside the lease areas, precisely during construction. Any GFW-based study of fishing activity around offshore wind is exposed to this, and the bias runs toward finding *increased* fishing exactly where and when one would look for displacement. Filtering on vessel name, as is common, does not remove it: one hull emits several name strings. **It establishes a reproducible baseline.** Sunrise Wind remains under construction and further Southern New England projects are permitted. This pipeline runs from committed inputs with no proprietary software, so the same analysis re-runs against future data as those projects progress. ## Reproducibility ::: {#provenance .cell execution_count=18} ``` {.python .cell-code} import esda, geopandas, libpysal, scipy print(f"geopandas {geopandas.__version__} libpysal {libpysal.__version__}") print(f"esda {esda.__version__} scipy {scipy.__version__}") print(f"seed {cfg.RANDOM_SEED} permutations {cfg.N_PERMUTATIONS} FDR alpha {cfg.FDR_ALPHA}") print(f"month denominator: {cfg.MONTH_DENOMINATOR}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` geopandas 1.1.4 libpysal 4.15.0 esda 2.10.0 scipy 1.18.1 seed 42 permutations 999 FDR alpha 0.05 month denominator: nominal ``` ::: ::: Exact package versions are pinned in `uv.lock`. Re-running this document reproduces every figure and table bit-for-bit; the Local Moran's permutations are seeded.
